key_insight: Common parameter initialization makes deep nets systematically overconfident; inserting a short, brain-inspired warm-up training phase with random noise substantially improves uncertainty calibration and the model's ability to recognize unknown inputs.
problem_solved: Addresses excessive model overconfidence and poor recognition of out-of-distribution/unknown inputs caused by standard initialization practices, which undermines reliable uncertainty estimates in deployed systems.
method: Add a brief warm-up training stage at the start of optimization where the network is trained with random noise (noise injection) before standard dataset training.
Show empirically that this warm-up reduces overconfident predictions and enhances calibration (reliability diagrams, expected calibration error) and meta-cognitive detection of unknown inputs.
Compare against standard initialization and calibration baselines to demonstrate consistent improvements with minimal added compute.
impact: A simple, low-cost modification to training pipelines that meaningfully improves predictive uncertainty and OOD awareness, making models safer and more trustworthy in real-world deployments.
visual_elements: Timeline diagram: training workflow showing a short 'warm-up with random noise' stage before regular training.
Reliability diagrams (before vs after) or confidence–accuracy curve illustrating reduced overconfidence and lower ECE.
Bar/line chart comparing OOD detection metrics (e.g., AUROC) and calibration scores across baselines and the proposed method.
Illustration/icon: brain + noise symbol to convey 'brain-inspired noise warm-up' and a shield icon for improved reliability/safety.
paper_title: Brain-inspired warm-up training with random noise for uncertainty calibration
